speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing difficulties conceiving and discomfort during sexual activity. To help you, please describe the specific nature of this discomfort and how long you have been trying to conceive.

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given your age, the duration of trying to conceive, and the specific symptoms of dyspareunia with pelvic floor tension, we need to evaluate for vaginismus or endometriosis. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Exam. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound. Do you have a history of painful periods or bowel/bladder issues?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vaginal Examination: No discharge. The initial attempt at speculum examination was aborted due to patient's pelvic floor muscles tensing up and discomfort. Pelvic Ultrasound: Normal uterus and adnexa with no evidence of fibroids or ovarian cysts.

speaker: Patient
text: All other systems reviewed are within normal limits. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Vulvodynia secondary to pelvic floor dysfunction, likely exacerbated by body dysmorphic disorder; the suggestion of multiple sclerosis is inconsistent with the clinical presentation of isolated pelvic pain and dyspareunia.
